Research Assistant / Associate in Health Data Science
Requisition ID:  29796
Location:  

Newcastle, GB

Contract Type:  Fixed Term
Working Pattern:  Full Time
Posted Date:  10 Nov 2026

 

Salary:

 

Research Assistance: £34,630 to £36,320 per annum

Research Associate: £37,369

 

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 8 December 2026 

 

The Role

 

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a major international project funded by the Wellcome Trust and led by Dr Emmanuel Molefi entitled “Diversity in Chronobiology: Discovering dynamics and interactions in chronobiology using multimodal, multiscale, and multinational data”. The project involves a 10-partner consortium across four continents; and you will be based at the CNNP Lab in the School of Computing at Newcastle University.

 

The aim of the project is to collect and curate a multimodal, multiscale, and multinational chronobiology and environmental health dataset; and use computational methods to understand how geographical, ethnical, cultural, and biological factors shape human biological rhythms in naturalistic settings.

 

As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles.pdf.  These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level.

 

Find out more about the Faculty of Science, Agriculture & Engineering (SAgE) here: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/sage/

 

Find out more about our Research Institutes: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/computing/research/groups/

 

Contact for the post is Dr Emmanuel Molefi (Emmanuel.Molefi@newcastle.ac.uk).

 

Duration of post is 12 months. 

 

To apply, please upload your CV and cover letter evidencing how your skills and experiences align to the person specification as outlined within the job description

 

Key Accountabilities

 

 

Research Assistant

 

Collect, analyse and interpret research data and draw conclusions on the outcomes.
Co-ordinate own work with that of others, use problem solving to affect the achievement of research objectives and contribute to the planning of the project(s).
Present information on research progress and outcomes to a Principal Investigator or groups overseeing the research project.
Write up results from own research activity and provide input into the research project’s dissemination, in whatever form (report, papers, chapters, books).
Use research resources (including, where required, laboratories, workshops and specialist equipment) as appropriate.

 

 

 

Research Associate

 

Contribute ideas, including enhancements to the technical or methodological aspects of the project.
Determine appropriate methodologies for research.
Assess research findings for the need/scope for further investigations.
Contribute to the writing up of the research and its dissemination, either through seminar and conference presentations or through publications.
Present research findings, either at conferences or through publications in reputable outlets appropriate to the discipline.
Contribute to grant applications submitted by others and develop own research objectives and proposals for funding.

 

 

 

The Person

 

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

 

Research Assistant

 

Experience analysing physiological, biomedical, or wearable sensor data
Experience applying machine learning, data-driven modelling, or multivariate methods to multimodal physiological and behavioral data
Experience in scientific software development and programming (e.g., MATLAB, Python, R)
Experience of developing and maintaining relationships with diverse stakeholders
Evidence of being able to conduct high quality research in one or more areas of Data Science, Machine Learning, Health Informatics, and Digital Health
Attention to detail and ability to work at high levels of accuracy
Ability to present complex information effectively to a range of audiences
Proven ability to analyse data and write-up results
Experience of working collaboratively with colleagues
Excellent IT skills in all major office applications
The ability to use personal initiative and creativity to solve research problems.

 

 

 

In addition for Research Associate

 

 

Awareness of the research environment
High level of analytical and problem solving capacity
Ability to communicate complex information with clarity
Experience of presentations at conferences and/or in high quality publications

 

 

 

 

Attributes and Behaviour

 

Commitment to working positively as a member of a multi-skilled research team
Ability to negotiate and prioritise multiple, competing responsibilities and to work to deadlines
Commitment to continued professional development
Understanding of good practice in equality, inclusion and diversity

 

 

 

Qualifications

 

 

Research Assistant

 

Honours degree in Health Data Science, Computer Science, Biomedical Informatics, Biomedical Engineering, Applied Mathematics / Statistics or a related discipline

 

 

 

In addition for Research Associate

 

PhD in Health Data Science, Computer Science, Biomedical Informatics, Biomedical Engineering, Applied Mathematics / Statistics or a related discipline

 

Newcastle University is a global University where everyone is treated with dignity and respect.  As a University of Sanctuary, we aim to provide a welcoming place of safety for all, offering opportunities to people fleeing violence and persecution.

 

We are committed to being a fully inclusive university which actively recruits, supports and retains colleagues from all sectors of society.  We value diversity as well as celebrate, support and thrive on the contributions of all of our employees and the communities they represent.  We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing teams, we believe that success is built on having teams whose backgrounds and experiences reflect the diversity of our university and student population.

 

At Newcastle University we hold a Gold Athena Swan award in recognition of our good employment practices for the advancement of gender equality.  We also hold a Race Equality Charter Bronze award in recognition of our work towards tackling race inequality in higher education REC.  We are a Disability Confident employer and will offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for the role as part of the offer and interview scheme.

 

In addition, we are a member of the Euraxess initiative supporting researchers in Europe.

 Opportunity Overview
 The University of Salford has a new opportunity for a Research Fellow in our state-of-the-art Energy House Labs. The successful candidate will join a UKRI-funded project testing new retrofit materials and manufacturing approaches at Energy House 2.0, one of the world's largest climate-controlled building research facilities. Inside its two environmental chambers, full-scale homes are tested under controlled conditions from -23°C to +53°C, with simulated wind, rain, snow and solar radiation.

 Working alongside the Energy House 2.0 Technical Director, you'll plan and run experiments on real buildings. That means designing test programmes; installing and managing sensor networks; carrying out in-situ measurements such as heat flux and U-values, whole-house heat transfer coefficient (HTC), airtightness and thermal imaging; and, assessing how retrofit measures change energy use, comfort and moisture risk. You'll then use that data to build, calibrate and validate building performance models, closing the gap between predicted and measured performance.

 You'll work directly with industry partners to test their products and systems, and turn the results into peer-reviewed publications, technical reports and clear evidence that manufacturers, stakeholders and policymakers can act on.

 We're looking for someone with a PhD (or equivalent postgraduate experience) in building physics, building engineering or a related field. You should have hands-on experience of experimental measurement and data analysis, and confidence with modelling or simulation tools. Above all, you'll need the collaborative skills to work across academic and industry teams.

 If you want your research to shape how the UK retrofits its homes, we'd like to hear from you. There are two fixed-term contracts available, one for 48 months and one for 53 months.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Ensure that all contractual, legal and financial processes are effectively managed with support of internal support services.

 Facilitate open communication and discussion between stakeholders, acting as subject matter expert developing, maintaining and working to stakeholder engagement plans and strategies.

 Lead research, under the supervision of the Technical Director and other co-Investigators. Lead research, under the supervision of the Technical Director and other co-Investigators.

 Collaboratively develop research working closing with the PIs, Co-I and other members of the Energy House Labs team.

 A bit about the Faculty
 The Faculty of Science, Engineering and Environment (SEE) is a centre of discovery and innovation. With a broad portfolio across computer sciences, engineering, built environment and human and natural sciences.

 Our Research and Innovation Centres work together to collaborate around the world’s greatest challenges including Net Zero, Climate Change and Resilience, Healthy Living and Industry. Our focus is on translating our pioneering research into real-world impact for people and industry and our research is recognised as world leading.

 With the largest group of research centres at the University, plus world-class test facilities such as Energy House 2.0, North of England Robotics Innovation Centre (NERIC), and the Acoustics Research Centre, we are at the forefront of pioneering discovery, nurturing the next generation of industry leaders.

Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) is a distinctive, unique institution, rooted in the Liverpool City Region and with a global presence. Our students and staff, past, present, and future, are the beating heart of our city and can be found in every corner of every industry and community. We couldn’t exist anywhere else and have shaped the city in which we belong. Working with the people of Liverpool to improve lives and support communities is at the heart of why we were founded and why we exist today.

The Faculty of Health, Innovation, Technology and Science is a pioneering Faculty, dedicated to creating and communicating knowledge and opportunities to ensure that all our students can excel within their chosen discipline.

The School of Computer Science and Mathematics is dedicated to producing research that has real-world application, boasting specialisms in immersive technologies, applications of artificial intelligence, trustworthy computing technologies and data science.

We are seeking to appoint a Research Associate in Artificial Intelligence to join the Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technologies Research Institute (AIDTRI).

AIDTRI brings together multidisciplinary expertise in AI and advanced digital technologies, with research spanning fundamental methodological development through to real-world application and evaluation. Key areas include AI, data science, trustworthy and explainable AI, causal AI, digital twins, immersive technologies, data visualisation and advanced computational modelling.

You will contribute to current AI and data science research programmes and to the development of new externally funded research.

Key activities will include:

conducting high-quality research in AI and Data Science;
organising, harmonising and analysing large, multimodal and multi-source datasets;
developing and evaluating AI methods;
collaborating with internal and external research partners;
preparing research papers and conference contributions;
contributing to external research funding applications; and
supporting research management and activities within AIDTRI.

You should hold a PhD in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a related discipline, or have submitted your thesis and be awaiting viva.

Essential criteria include experience of conducting and publishing high-quality AI research, strong knowledge of AI algorithms, programming experience in Python, R or similar, excellent communication and organisational skills, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

Experience with large and complex AI problems, novel AI or computational methods, advanced Python programming, and research funding proposals would be advantageous.

You should clearly demonstrate in your supporting statement how you meet all essential criteria in the person specification, providing specific evidence and examples for each criterion. Evidence against the desirable criteria should also be provided where applicable.

We anticipate holding interviews the second week of December 2026.

Further information about AIDTRI is available at:
https://www.ljmu.ac.uk/research/centres-and-institutes/artificial-intelligence-and-digital-technologies-research-institute

For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Professor Ivan Olier, Head of AIDTRI, at I.Olier@ljmu.ac.uk.

In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction, and development support as well as family-friendly policies.

This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do. Find out more about working at LJMU here. 

If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you. 

The Faculty of Health, Innovation, Technology and Science is committed to promoting equality and diversity, including the Athena SWAN Gender Equality charter for promoting the career of Women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) in higher education. We particularly welcome applications from women for this post and all appointments will be made on merit. Please let us know if you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process.

Please note all of our vacancies will be closed to applications at midnight on the advertised closing date, unless otherwise stated.

LJMU are committed to adhering to the Principles set out in the Researcher Development Concordat; in line with this all fixed-term researchers will be supported to complete 10 days professional development activities per year (pro-rata).

 Postdoctoral Research Associate in Smart and Green AI

 Northeastern University London

 Location:  London, Devon House (St Katherines Dock)

 Term:  1.5 years, fixed term, full-time

 Reports to:  Professor Bipin Rajendran

 Benefits:  The university supports staff maintaining a good work-life balance, offering: ( i ) flexible working and parental leave opportunities; ( ii ) an employee assistance programme which provides free, confidential advice on both home and work concerns, as well as optional private medical insurance; ( iii ) season ticket loans; and ( iv ) being part of the cycle-to-work scheme.

 Start:  January 2027 

 The Role   

 Northeastern University London invites applications for a Post-doctoral Research Associate (PDRA) in Smart and Green AI to work with Professor Bipin Rajendran as part of his UKRI fellowship grant. 

 The successful candidate will work on the design, implementation and validation of hardware accelerator prototypes for state-of-the-art energy efficient and trustworthy AI models based on neuromorphic computing and In-Memory Computing (IMC) principles. 

 Core duties include:

 Contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of neuromorphic and in-memory hardware accelerator prototype boards for training and inference of state-of-the-art AI models.

 Develop algorithms, architectures, and hardware–software co-design methodologies for energy-efficient AI computation on neuromorphic and in-memory computing (IMC) platforms.

 Collaborate with cross-disciplinary teams spanning hardware design, AI/ML algorithms, information theory, and systems software to enable end-to-end system integration and validation.

 Publish high-quality research outcomes in leading journals and conferences in neuromorphic computing, AI hardware, and computer architecture.

 Support the supervision and mentoring of PhD and MSc students within the research group.

 Engage with industrial and academic collaborators to support joint research activities, technology transfer, and translational impact.

 Contribute to project management activities, including technical reporting, proposal development, and dissemination of research outcomes. 

 We particularly encourage applications from those belonging to groups underrepresented in UK higher education. 

 About the Institute 

 The Intelligent Networked Systems Institute (INSI) at NU London is a newly established transatlantic research hub focused on next-generation connectivity and intelligent computing and learning systems. The INSI London Hub acts as a bridge between the US and Europe, advancing interdisciplinary collaboration across continents. INSI is dedicated to addressing pressing challenges in telecommunications, artificial intelligence, quantum information, and information processing—all with the objective of creating a more efficient, connected, and secure world. 

 About the University 

 Founded in 2012, Northeastern University London (formerly known as New College of the Humanities) has established itself as a prestigious higher education institution based in the heart of London. Northeastern University London is part of Northeastern University’s Global Campus Network. Positioned as top ranking in the USA, Northeastern has campuses in Arlington, Boston, Charlotte, Miami, Oakland, San Jose, and Seattle in the USA, and Toronto and Vancouver in Canada.

 After becoming part of Northeastern University’s global network in early 2019, the University has undergone a period of rapid growth, having been granted Taught Degree Awarding Powers in February 2020 and moved to a new, state-of-the-art campus in 2021.  

 Northeastern University London offers a vibrant, collegiate community delivering broad and academically rigorous degree programmes, designed to equip graduates with the combination of skills and knowledge that are increasingly desired by organisations, employers, and society. It offers state of the art audio visual technology in its teaching and meeting spaces across the organisation. 

 Person Specification Criteria   

 To undertake this role, the following should apply – should you not have the experience below, please do highlight where transferable skills would assist with you undertaking the role. 

 Qualifications  

 PhD in Computer Science, Electronics or Computer Engineering or related quantitative field.   

 Key Criteria   

 Strong publication record in neuromorphic hardware design demonstrated through publications in leading conferences and/or journals, with expertise extending beyond materials and device optimisation toward system-, architecture-, and algorithm-level innovation.

 Experience in characterisation, modelling, and testing of nanoscale memristive and/or emerging non-volatile memory devices, including board-level integration and experimental evaluation of such devices.

 Experience in the simulation, implementation, and validation of state-of-the-art machine learning models, e.g., probabilistic, neuromorphic, Transformer, and/or state-space models, with an ability to translate algorithms into implementations suitable for emerging hardware platforms.

 Experience with FPGA-based test boards and hardware prototyping for emerging AI hardware systems, including the implementation and testing of algorithms on platforms incorporating emerging memory technologies such as STT-RAM and/or memristive devices.

 Experience in hardware–software co-design approaches aimed at mitigating, exploiting, or adapting to the non-ideal effects and variability of nanoscale devices, with an emphasis on developing robust algorithms and system-level solutions for real-world hardware.

 Effective communication (oral and written) skills, with the ability to write research reports and papers in a style accessible to academic audiences.

 Ability to work independently and as part of a team on research programmes   

 Additional Information   

 Enquiries  

 Informal enquiries may be made to Professor Bipin Rajendran (b.rajendran@nulondon.ac.uk). However, all applications must be made in accordance with the application process specified. 

 Application Process   

 Applications should be made via the ' Apply ' button above by 23:59 on 25 November 2026. Please reference your application “ R143238 ”. 

 Applications must include a CV and covering letter of no more than one page that addresses the criteria for the role and includes names and contact information of up to three references. References will only be sought for short-listed candidates. 

 You may upload your CV and Cover letter as a single document if you are unable to upload them individually.  

 Participation in the equal opportunities section is encouraged, but voluntary. 

 Interviews are expected to take place between 26 November and 30 November 2026.   

 The panel will be shortlisting for this position on a rolling basis so please apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close this post before the closing date if we receive a large number of applications.   

 Please note this role may require a basic or enhanced DBS check. Our organisation acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard, protect and promote the welfare of our students and staff, and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities, government guidance and complies with best practice and Ofsted requirements. You must adhere to the above if you are offered a role with NU London. 

 Applications are welcome from all sections of the community and will be judged on merit alone. We welcome applications from underrepresented groups. Candidates must be able to demonstrate their eligibility to work in the UK in accordance with the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006. 

 Job sponsorship . Visa sponsorship may be available for a successful candidate for this position.

 You will join the 2D-MINDs team, led by Dr Soumya Sarkar within the Sustainable Electronic Technologies research group in the School of Electronics and Computer Science (ECS) at the University of Southampton. You will also be part of the interdisciplinary ECS Centre for Neuromorphic Technologies (CeNT).

 The position is funded by the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship “2D semiconductors for intelligent non-volatile memory devices” (2DMINDs) . The post will be full-time for a period until 31/01/2029 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for another 12 months.   You will investigate two-dimensional semiconductors and ferroelectric materials to develop non-volatile memory that co-locates storage and processing for low-power AI hardware. Your research will combine materials characterisation, interface engineering and device fabrication at Southampton Nanofabrication Centre to develop foundry-compatible fabrication protocols alongside specialist electrical and optical characterisation facilities. Training and support will be provided to develop the skills required for your research.

 The role is well suited to candidates who wish to develop their expertise in emerging memory devices and neuromorphic technologies within a supportive, interdisciplinary research environment. We welcome applicants with complementary experimental backgrounds; experience across all the areas listed below is not expected.

 You should be a resourceful and passionate researcher who will plan and conduct experiments, develop measurement techniques and generate high-quality research data. You will contribute to the project’s scientific direction, prepare manuscripts, undertake short research visits to project partners (University of Cambridge, NPL), present findings at international conferences, write project reports and support the supervision of master’s and PhD students.

 The role offers support for conference travel, collaboration, industry engagement and outreach. Extensive leadership training and transferable skills development will support your progression towards research independence and future leadership in ferroelectric neuromorphic devices.

 Essential requirements 

 A PhD, or near completion of a PhD, in materials science, physics, electronic engineering or a related discipline.

 Experience in one or more of the following: fabrication and characterisation of devices based on 2D semiconductors, or ferroelectric materials.

 Strong experimental and analytical skills, with the ability to plan research, interpret results and solve technical problems.

 Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams.

 Desirable experience 

 Ferroelectric transistors, tunnel junctions or diodes, or other non-volatile memory and neuromorphic devices.

 E-beam lithography, thin-film deposition or dry-transfer assembly of van der Waals heterostructures.

'Research Technician – Immunofluorescence and Tissue Imaging (Full-Time/Part-time)

Job id: 162905. Salary: £39,755 - £44,685 per annum inclusive of London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 11 November 2026. Closing date: 29 November 2026.

Business unit: Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine. Department: Institute of Pharmaceutical Science.

Contact details: Dr Heba Sailem. Heba.sailem@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Waterloo Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About Us

The Sailem Group is a multidisciplinary research team working to understand cancer biology and improve personalised cancer treatment. Our research brings together experimental, computational and data-driven approaches to study tumour heterogeneity, the tumour microenvironment and treatment response, with the aim of identifying predictive biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets.

A major focus of the group is the development and application of computational and AI approaches to complex biomedical data, including tissue imaging, genomics and clinical data. We are now expanding our experimental capabilities in tissue imaging to enable detailed investigation of the cellular composition and spatial organisation of tumours.

This position is central to developing that experimental capability. The successful candidate will focus primarily on hands-on laboratory research, particularly immunofluorescence, FFPE tissue staining, antibody optimisation and advanced tissue imaging.

The role would therefore particularly suit someone who enjoys experimental science, method development and troubleshooting, and who is motivated by seeing high-quality experimental work contribute to biological discovery and clinically relevant cancer research.

About The Role

Our research focuses on understanding how the tumour microenvironment influences cancer progression and treatment response, and on identifying potential therapeutic targets. Multiplex tissue imaging will provide an important experimental approach for addressing these questions by revealing the cellular composition and spatial organisation of tumours.

The postholder will drive the experimental development and application of multiplex immunofluorescence, from selecting and optimising antibodies and developing robust multiplex panels through to generating high-quality spatial tissue data. The role provides an opportunity to build specialist expertise in cutting-edge imaging technologies, solve challenging experimental problems, and contribute directly to biological discoveries and clinically relevant research.

Working independently, the postholder will be responsible for experimental optimisation, quality control and troubleshooting. They will work with Dr Sailem on research questions, experimental priorities and interpretation of findings.

The postholder will contribute to scientific discoveries and research outputs arising from this work, including presentations and publications. There may also be opportunities to apply their specialist expertise to collaborative research projects.

This is a full time role however part-time applications will be considered (at least 16 hours per week), you will be offered an a fixed term 12 months contract until 31st December 2027.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

BSc/MSc or equivalent experience in biomedical science, biology, immunology, biochemistry or a related discipline.
Substantial hands-on experience in IF/IHC on FFPE tissue, including tissue handling, staining and fluorescence microscopy/digital pathology.
Experience in antibody optimisation and validation, including titration, controls, specificity assessment and troubleshooting.
Ability to work independently and proactively solve experimental problems, including developing, optimising, quality-controlling and troubleshooting complex experimental workflows with minimal supervision.
Ability to independently manage and prioritise multiple research projects, working effectively with researchers to understand requirements and deliver experimental work.
Strong laboratory organisation and quality-management skills, including rigorous experimental documentation and management of samples and reagents.

Desirable criteria

Experience developing, optimising or implementing multiplex tissue-imaging assays, ideally multiplex immunofluorescence, with experience of Cell DIVE or a comparable highly multiplexed imaging platform.
Experience in quantitative image analysis of tissue imaging data, including segmentation, marker quantification and/or spatial analysis.
Experience conducting literature searches and applying published evidence to develop or optimise experimental protocols and antibody panels.
Experience contributing to scientific publications, including analysis and interpretation of experimental data, preparation of figures and/or manuscript writing.

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

AI Vision and Automation Engineer (KTP Associate) - Full Time, Fixed Term up to 24 months duration

This post is funded through a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) between Harper Adams University and Karsten UK Limited, a fresh citrus processing and distribution business supplying major UK and European retailers. The Associate will develop and embed an AI-driven vision and quality sorting capability at Karsten UK’s Newport facility. A Fanuc Delta pick-and-place robot, already owned by Karsten UK, provides the actuation platform. The system will inspect and grade fruit against retailer specifications, using a compact conveyor training rig. The KTP funds the vision and training components, not the robot.

Working from the conveyor training rig, the Associate will develop a Discrete Element Method (DEM) simulation model of fruit dynamics. The Associate will build a photorealistic rendering pipeline to generate synthetic training images with automated annotation, and train AI classification models to achieve 95% accuracy using synthetic data alone. Integration with the robot controller will then translate classification outputs into pick-and-place sorting. The training method is product-agnostic and can be retrained for new products and specifications.

The role combines AI model development, simulation-driven data generation, robotic integration, and practical engineering delivery in a food processing environment. Employment will be full-time at Karsten UK’s Newport facility, directed day to day by the site team. The Associate will receive at least half a day per week of academic supervision from Harper Adams University, with access to its Collaborative Simulation Laboratory. Development, training, and validation will take place on the conveyor training rig beside production, and live production will be reached only after validation on the rig. The post is a 24-month fixed-term appointment, with a target start date of Monday 25 January 2027.

The appointee will also be expected to:

Develop and deliver training programmes for production and maintenance personnel. These will embed the vision and sorting capability within Karsten UK’s operational teams. Performance monitoring dashboards and continuous improvement protocols will be established to sustain system performance. Commercial benefits, including throughput improvement and value recovery from more accurate grading, will be quantified and reported. Technical reports, academic publications, and a project case study will be prepared in accordance with KTP programme requirements, and progress will be presented at regular Local Management Committee meetings involving academic and industrial supervisors. The appointee will comply with the health and safety, food safety, data management, and intellectual property policies of both Harper Adams University and Karsten UK Limited.

 

Experience/Qualifications:

Essential:

A first or upper second-class honours degree in Computer Science, Electronic Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a closely related discipline. Demonstrable experience developing and training AI or machine learning models for image classification or object detection. Proven programming or model-development experience in Python and/or MATLAB & Simulink, including scripting for data processing, model training, and automation workflows. Understanding of computer vision principles including image formation, lighting, and camera calibration. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage complex technical work independently and within a team.

Desirable:

A postgraduate qualification (MSc or PhD) in a relevant engineering, computer science, robotics, or automation discipline. Experience with physics-based simulation tools such as DEM, FEA, CFD, or multibody dynamics software. Familiarity with photorealistic rendering software such as Blender or KeyShot for synthetic data generation. Knowledge of industrial control systems, PLC programming, or robot programming. Practical experience integrating vision or machine learning outputs with robotic, automation, or mechatronic hardware. A background in food processing, agricultural, or manufacturing environments. Familiarity with version control systems and collaborative software development practices. Prior industrial placement or collaborative research demonstrating delivery of practical outcomes.

For further information about the University or to see full job description, please visit our website at www.harper-adams.ac.uk

Application Procedure:

All applications should be completed and submitted using the Harper Adams e-Recruitment programme at http://jobs.harper-adams.ac.uk. Applications must be completed no later than Tuesday 8 December 2026.

Applicants must complete the full application, submit a CV and a cover letter. A structured statement addressing each criterion in the person specification should be included. The online application questions also form part of the assessment. Both the statement and the answers will be assessed as part of the shortlisting process.

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend an in-person interview at Karsten UK Limited, Suite 3, Nova House, Audley Avenue Enterprise Park, Newport, Shropshire, TF10 7DW on Wednesday 16 December 2026. No remote interviews will be conducted. The interview will include a 7-minute candidate presentation, a structured competency-based interview, and a separate informal conversation with a Karsten UK staff member, which forms part of the selection process. The presentation topic will be provided to candidates in advance of the interview date.

For adjustments to your application, contact vacancies@harper-adams.ac.uk.

If you are seeking sponsorship for a Skilled Worker visa, please visit https://www.gov.uk/browse/visas-immigration for further information.

About the role

We are seeking a Post-Doctoral Researcher to join our Centre for Nutrition, Exercise & Metabolism (CNEM), specifically to work on the Bath MyoRhythms Project - a BBSRC-funded experiment into the effects of exercise timing on metabolic rhythms in human skeletal muscle. 

The individual appointed to this role will be responsible for co-ordinating tissue analysis across multiple international sites with our project collaborators, leading on biochemical analysis of tissue samples at Bath, collating and analysing all resultant data and contributing to the writing of manuscripts for publication. 

This individual would be working within our centre of around 35-40 individuals, with opportunity to mentor PhD students and contribute to the overall organisation of CNEM.

Analytical skills in the biochemistry laboratory will be essential. This will include processing human tissue samples (i.e. blood and skeletal muscle) and conducting relevant assays, including Enzyme-Linked ImmunoSorbent Assays (ELISA), multiplex assays (MSD), automated spectrophotometric assays (Randox Daytona) and Western blotting.

The Smuts Management Committee invites applications for a non-renewable Smuts Visiting Research Fellowship in Commonwealth Studies, tenable for 9 months commencing from 1st October 2027.

The Smuts Memorial Fund usually elects one Smuts Visiting Research Fellow a year to come to Cambridge to carry out research for up to 9 months. These Fellowships are intended for mid- to senior career academics, of international calibre in an institutional position and who received their PhD at least five years prior to the application closing date.

Fellows may come from any nationality, but should be normally resident outside the United Kingdom, and a wide variety of disciplines in the social sciences, arts and humanities. They are expected to advance Commonwealth Studies in Cambridge mainly by pursuing research, but also by taking part in seminars and similar activities within the University. During the tenure of their Fellowship, Fellows are required to deliver at least one public lecture in Cambridge arranged in consultation with the Managers of the Smuts Memorial Fund.

Commonwealth Studies is defined here as research that is focused on past or present countries and/or issues pertaining to one or more parts of the Commonwealth. Fellows will have access, by agreement, to the holdings of Faculty and Departmental libraries, to the libraries of the Centres of African Studies and South Asian Studies and to the University Library, which houses the extensive collection of materials relating to the history of the British Empire and Commonwealth, formerly housed in the Royal Commonwealth Society Library in London.

The Managers expect that the person appointed would be intending to come to Cambridge to work on a project that builds on existing research for which a period of residence in Cambridge is demonstrably appropriate, although they would not rule out a new piece of work that is expected to be completed by the end of the 9-month tenure of the Fellowship.

The closing date for applications is the 11th December 2026. Applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application in February 2027.

Role Description

About the Role

In many parts of the world, excessive use of phosphorus (P) fertilizers in agricultural soil has led to large-scale contamination of the environment. On the other hand, in other areas, P deficient soils and poor access to fertilizers present a major constraint to crop production. Warmer, drier conditions resulting from climate change will exacerbate these problems as low soil moisture reduces plant-availability of P. In natural systems, most plants rely on root symbioses with mutualistic mycorrhizal fungi for efficient P uptake. These interactions remain active in major crop species. However, the delicate balance between plant and fungal partner is far from optimised for both intensive and less-intensive agricultural systems.

In the 3-year project to which this role will contribute, we will characterise plant genetic mechanisms that coordinate the interaction of mycorrhizal fungi with plant P and water status, the development of the root system and the broader community of soil microbes. With partners at Cambridge University and in Germany and the US, we will work from the scale of the single gene to field evaluation to define a framework for rational optimization of plant-mycorrhizal symbioses for more efficient P use in agriculture. The modelling component will involve combining existing models of root system growth, rhizosphere processes and P uptake developed by the project partners, and developing new models of the effects and costs of mycorrhizal symbioses.

About You

You will be educated to doctoral level in a relevant subject and have experience of research in plant and soil science using both qualitative and quantitative methods. You will have experience in mathematical modelling of plant-soil systems and basic-level programming. You will understand the plant and soil science behind the project and be able to translate that into models using the results of the experimental work. You will have excellent oral and written communication skills and ability to collaborate across disciplines.

About Us

As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield’s world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here.

The Environment and Agrifood Theme combines research groups with more than 50 years of experience in the challenges of sustainability, natural capital management and future food systems. It includes the Centre for Soil, Agrifood and Biosciences which has expertise in soil, plant and microbial systems across scales, with the Cranfield Environment Centre which has expertise in environmental informatics and modelling, and is the UK National Reference Centre for soil.

Our Values and Commitments

Our shared, stated values help to define who we are and underpin everything we do: Ambition; Impact; Respect; and Community. Find out more here.

We aim to create and maintain a culture in which everyone can work and study together and realise their full potential. We are a Disability Confident Employer. We are committed to actively exploring flexible working options for each role and have been ranked in the Top 30 family friendly employers in the UK by the charity Working Families. Find out more about our key commitments to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Flexible Working here.

Working Arrangements

Collaborating and connecting are integral to so much of what we do. Our Working Arrangements Framework provides many staff with the opportunity to flexibly combine on-site and remote working, where job roles allow, balancing the needs of our community of staff, students, clients and partners.

How to apply                                   

For an informal discussion about this opportunity, please contact Guy Kirk, Professor of Soil Systems, on (E): g.kirk@cranfield.ac.uk

Apply online now. Please do not hesitate to contact us for further details on E: peoplerecruitment@cranfield.ac.uk. Please quote reference number 5434.

 This post represents an exciting opportunity for an ambitious individual to join a research team in Keele University’s School of Life Sciences . The Postdoctoral Research Associate position forms part of a UKRI Future Leader Fellowship research project within the Arbovirus (arthropod-borne viruses) Refractory Team. Our team focuses on utilizing knowledge on how viruses function in our effort to stop their dissemination. We use genetic modification of both viruses and mosquitoes in an effort to develop novel technologies to control arbovirus transmission independent of conventional insecticides.

 The successful candidate will take the lead on one of the work packages forming a UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship research programme aiming to reduce the burden of mosquito-borne infectious diseases. In particular, this part of the project aims to further our knowledge of insect specific viruses (ISVs) and explore their potential as biotechnology tool. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop a range of laboratory and analytical skills, strengthen their personal professional development through courses and workshops as well as visiting one of our project partners in Estonia for hands-on training in one of the leading Alphavirus research laboratories.

 Routine tasks of the successful candidate will involve molecular and virology techniques, plasmid design and cloning, mosquito maintenance and mosquito transgenesis as well as mosquito-virus interaction studies at Containment Level 2. They will be joining a dynamic and interactive team of researchers with a passion for virus research and science in general. The successful candidate will ideally have experience working with Hazard Group 2 pathogenic viruses, be proficient in a range of molecular and cell culture techniques and be able to come up with creative and innovative solutions to research challenges. Please note: this job is only available to current employees of Lancaster University

We are seeking to appoint a full-time Research Associate or Senior Research Associate  until March 2029, with the possibility of further extension.  This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing research programme using real-world contact data and mathematical modelling to understand how infectious diseases spread and the potential impact of different control measures. The work will focus predominantly on two uniquely rich datasets, one capturing general population contact patterns during the COVID-19 pandemic using large-scale contact tracing data, and one focused specifically on school-aged children, to help shape public health policy on disease control both in schools and more broadly. The successful candidate will join Lancaster Medical School and work closely with Dr Jonathan Read and Dr Trystan Leng.

We welcome applications from researchers with a PhD in (or equivalent experience) in infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical modelling, quantitative social science, or a related discipline. The postholder will clean and analyse contact patterns from two distinct datasets: 1) the NHS/UKHSA contact tracing data from England, collected during the COVID-19 pandemic and 2) data collected from the School and Community Connections study, a bespoke study which will collect data specifically for this analysis, aimed at understanding the contact patterns of schoolchildren. Further, the postholder will use transmission-dynamic models informed by this contact data alongside surveillance data, fitted using Bayesian methods, to undertake scenario-based mathematical modelling of the potential impact of a range of public health interventions, as well as exploring the usefulness of contact data in explaining observed patterns of incidence.

Depending on experience, the postholder may also contribute to survey design and data collection during the School and Community Connections Study.

The post is funded jointly through a MRC grant awarded to Dr Read and through Dr Leng's Wellcome Early Career Award 'Control without closure: school-level approaches for pathogen control within and between schools': https://wellcome.org/research-funding/funding-portfolio/funded-grants/control-without-closure-school-level-approaches

You will liaise with colleagues within Lancaster Medical School (Dr Sam Moore) alongside external partners, including Prof Henrik Salje (University of Cambridge), Prof Moritz Kraemer (University of Oxford), colleagues at UKHSA, and the UK government’s Department for Education science team.

You will be expected to be based at Lancaster University, however, we can consider remote working within the UK. There is also the opportunity for a longer-term research visit to external partners’ institutions.  We welcome applications from candidates seeking flexible working requests.

Worldwide, three people are diagnosed with encephalitis every minute—and autoimmune/immune-mediated causes are now just as common as infectious ones. While earlier immunotherapy often resolves acute symptoms like seizures, children remain disproportionately affected by devastating, long-term neuropsychiatric and sleep disorders.

We are seeking an ambitious Postdoctoral Researcher to join a Wellcome-funded programme bridging this critical research gap. You will use preclinical experimental disease models and advanced electrophysiology to uncover how acute synaptic and neuro-immune disruptions drive persistent brain network changes—and identify new therapeutic targets to improve long-term outcomes for children. Working closely with an embedded clinical research team collecting longitudinal neuroimaging and cognitive data in children and young people, you will form part of a truly translational team.

Investigate Circuit Function: Perform whole-cell patch clamp and local field potential recordings to uncover synaptic and circuit dysfunction.
Capture Live Network Activity: Conduct stereotaxic surgeries to implant wireless EEG transmitters and osmotic pumps, analysing in vivo network connectivity and sleep/behavioural phenotypes.
Explore Neuro-Immune Crosstalk: Investigate how microglia and disrupted neuro-immune signalling drive persistent structural and network changes, contributing to complementary molecular analyses.
Manage Colony Operations: Oversee a genetically modified colony (breeding, genotyping, and accurate record-keeping) in strict compliance with Home Office regulations.
Share Impact & Foster a Positive Research Culture: Publish in peer-reviewed journals, present at international conferences, and engage with stakeholders and the public, while supporting a safe, inclusive, and sustainable lab environment.

You will hold a PhD in neuroscience, physiology, pharmacology, or a related discipline. About the role

Supported by BBSRC funding, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join the group of Dr Rachel Lai at Imperial College London. This 48-month position, available from January 2027, will investigate how metabolic rewiring and cellular ion fluxes govern innate immune responses and inflammation.

Macrophages are essential sentinels of innate immunity, but their dysregulated activation drives severe inflammatory diseases. Macrophage activation requires the convergence of biophysical and biochemical inputs, including acute metabolic shifts, ionic fluxes and oxidative stress. Working within a dynamic, multi-institutional team, you will employ biological and analytical assays and tools to define the physiological checkpoints that determine how macrophages integrate these stress signals and transition from homeostasis to a proinflammatory state.

 

What you would be doing

You will lead studies investigating how metabolic and ionic shifts govern macrophage activation, taking responsibility for experimental planning and execution, data analysis and manuscript preparation. Working closely with members of the Lai group and collaborators across the multi-institutional team, you will develop and apply experimental approaches to deliver the project’s scientific aims.
You will also supervise and train students, share expertise with colleagues and contribute to the day-to-day running of the laboratory.
You will present findings at scientific conferences, prepare reports for research funders and contribute to future grant applications.

What we are looking for

We are looking for a highly motivated and collaborative scientist with:

A PhD in Immunology, Physiology, Cell Biology or a closely related discipline.
Practical experience with primary macrophages or relevant cell-culture models, with strong knowledge of innate immunity and macrophage biology.
Experience studying immunometabolism or cellular physiology, including functional immunology and biochemical assays.
Ability to lead independent research and work collaboratively, with experience in experimental planning, data analysis and scientific writing.

 

Experience in one or more of the following is highly desirable but not essential: measuring cellular ion fluxes or transporter/channel activity, mass spectrometry-based proteomics or metabolomics, bioinformatics or computational analysis of omics datasets, or working with small-animal models. Holding a relevant UK personal licence would also be advantageous.

This is a full-time (35 hours per week), fixed-term post for 48 months. The expected start date is mid-January 2027.

Are you interested in translational rheumatology research? Do you want to better understand and treat pain in inflammatory arthritis? Would you like to be trained by and work with leading rheumatologists, pain biologists and immunologists?

We are looking to recruit a clinical fellow to join the Arthritis UK research consortium TOPPIA: Targeting of Peripheral Pain in Inflammatory Arthritis focused on peripheral pain in inflammatory arthritis.

The TOPPIA consortium is directed by Prof Leonie Taams and Prof Franziska Denk at King’s College London, and comprises basic and clinician scientists, lived experience partners and policy experts from King’s College London, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, King’s College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, University College London, Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust, Cardiff University, University of Oxford, University of Birmingham, University of Glasgow, and The Rockefeller University in the USA.

Together, the TOPPIA consortium will seek to identify new treatment targets for inflammatory arthritis pain, create a biobank of joint samples to study clinical information on pain, improve tailored diagnosis and care and advocate for pain to be prioritised in care and research.

About the role

We are looking to recruit a Clinical Fellow to study for a PhD degree under the supervision of Prof Leonie Taams at King’s College London and Dr Fran Humby at GSTT as part of a large Arthritis UK research consortium TOPPIA: Targeting of Peripheral Pain in Inflammatory Arthritis aimed at studying the drivers of persistent pain in inflammatory arthritis.

You will be responsible for patient recruitment, conduct clinical assessments including pain phenotyping of patients, perform ultrasound-guided synovial tissue biopsies as well as be involved in cutting-edge investigations of synovial tissue samples in the lab. You will also help ensure harmonisation of data and sample collection across the consortium.

The clinical aspects of the work will take place in the Rheumatology Department at Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Trust (GSTT), which is one of the biggest departments in the country.

The laboratory work will be done in the Centre for Inflammation Biology & Cancer Immunology, in close collaboration with the lab of Prof Franziska Denk, on the Guy’s Campus.

The successful candidate will need to have a strong track record in rheumatology, demonstrable interest in translational research in inflammatory arthritis, experience in wet-lab or dry-lab research and strong analytical skills. A pro-active attitude, excellent attention to detail, excellent data analysis and record keeping skills as well as strong interpersonal, communication and time management skills are essential. You should be able to communicate and liaise effectively with a wide range of partners and patients. The expectation is that you will work towards a PhD degree as part of your appointment.

This is a full-time post (40 hours per week), but part-time working (minimal 80%) could be considered. You will be offered a fixed term contract of 36 months. The fellowship will cover salary, PhD fees (at the UK level), and research expenses.

Please note that this post is open only to applicants with UK/Home fee status (usually demonstrated by holding a British passport or settled status) and not requiring ATAS.

 Our vision is of a world better led, a world better served and a world better governed. We are a global school committed to improving the quality of government and public policymaking worldwide, through three routes: teaching current and future leaders ; generating research with impact ; and engaging with governments and practitioners .

 What we offer 

 The School is a collaborative, friendly, and dynamic department based in an award-winning building in Oxford. We host regular events and talks with well-known guest speakers – all of which are open to staff. On the social side, we have a regular events calendar that are designed to appeal to all, including our Christmas and summer parties.

 As an employer, we genuinely care about our employees’ wellbeing and this is reflected in the range of benefits that we offer including:

 Cycle loan scheme and discounted bus travel and Season Ticket travel loans

 The postholder will undertake a focused review of academic and policy literature on medical workforce expansion, drawing on international experience to identify lessons relevant to Nigeria. Research activities may include volunteer recruitment, analysis of health and genomic data using genetic epidemiology, trial emulation or health economic methods to investigate cardiometabolic disease risk, disease trajectories, treatment response and long-term health outcomes in diverse populations. Opportunities to contribute to qualitative and health services research on improving inclusion and representation in research may also be available.

About You

You will bring a strong clinical background as a doctor, pharmacist, nurse or allied health professional. Research experience is desirable but not essential, but the ability to think critically and develop scientific hypotheses and research plans is required. You will be self-disciplined, organised and passionate about your work, and about delivering improvements in health through research that effectively engages with and includes people from underrepresented backgrounds.

The Institute is organised into six research centres which, following the Institute strategic plan, also have Centre-specific objectives.

We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form.

 Strathclyde Institute of Pharmacy and Biomedical Sciences is seeking to appoint a Research Associate to a project awarded funding from the FDA (BAA Number: FY26C1AP5). As a Research Associate, under the guidance of Professor Hannah Batchelor, you will play a lead role in the delivery of this project.

 The Research Associate will contribute to the development and validation of paediatric-specific TIM protocols coupled with mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling. The role will support a regulatory science project designed to establish an evidence-based in vitro workflow for predicting paediatric oral drug performance.

 The project applies TIM technology in a new regulatory context: paediatrics. This will require protocol redesign, selection of age-appropriate physiological parameters, careful alignment with clinical reference datasets, and verification of outputs against relevant clinical pharmacokinetic data.
The successful candidate will take day-to-day responsibility for planning, managing and delivering the project. This will require an integrated programme of experimental work using the TIM-1 apparatus, analytical method development and application (including HPLC), structured literature searching, and evidence synthesis. The postholder will use published evidence to inform protocol design and experimental decisions, and will identify, source and extract relevant data from published clinical studies to enable comparison with and interpretation of the experimental outputs.
You will develop and implement analytical methods, evidence-based experimental protocols, standard operating procedures and reporting approaches. You will take technical ownership of selected equipment and be expected to drive the project proactively, monitor progress against milestones and expenditure, manage risks and competing priorities, and ensure delivery to the agreed programme and budget.

 You will communicate progress, emerging findings, risks and decisions clearly and regularly to the funding partner and other stakeholders, and prepare the required technical reports and presentations. You will also write up research for publication, individually or with colleagues, disseminate findings through peer-reviewed publications and conferences, and engage with external networks to share evidence and inform the continuing development of the research objectives.

 To be considered for the role, you will be educated to a minimum of PhD level in an appropriate discipline, or have significant relevant experience in addition to a relevant degree. You will have sufficient breadth or depth of knowledge in advanced dissolution methodology; experience of analytical techniques and a working knowledge of PBPK software and a developing ability to conduct individual research work, to disseminate results and to prepare research reports. You will have an ability to plan and organise your own workload effectively and an ability to work within a team environment. You will have excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to listen, engage and persuade, and to present complex information in an accessible way to a range of audiences.

 Whilst a Post-Doctoral Research Associate is ideally sought for this position; applications from candidates who are close to PhD completion or whose award is pending, are welcome. In such circumstances, the appointment will be made at Research Assistant level (grade 6) and duties will be adjusted to reflect the grade of the post. This will continue until the PhD award is confirmed, at which point the duties and grade will be revised accordingly

For any informal enquiries, please contact Professor Hannah Batchelor ( hannah.batchelor@strath.ac.uk ).

Research Assistant (0.6 FTE)
Department
Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology and Dynamics
Salary
£40,784 to £45,173 per annum pro rata inclusive
Closing Date
Tuesday 24 November 2026
Reference
EPH-EPED-2026-10

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice.

The post-holder will be a member of the team delivering the Lancet Commission: ‘Rethinking Misinformation, Health and Human Security’, led by Prof. Heidi Larson. 

The Commission comprises an international group of Commissioners to develop approaches addressing misinformation. Working closely with the Commission co-chairs /working group (WG) leads, the post-holder will provide research, analytical and coordination support, alongside stakeholder engagement and dissemination of findings. 

Responsibilities include:

Coordinate WGs, including managing meetings, supporting delivery against deadlines and milestones, and helping to ensure coherence across workstreams;
Contribute (as defined by WG leads) to research activities (e.g., case studies) and the development of engagement and dissemination outputs (e.g., working papers, policy briefs, peer-reviewed publications) and activities. 
Contribute to the development and final synthesis of the Lancet Commission report.

We seek an applicant with experience or a strong interest in researching misinformation, trust, information systems and health; who is comfortable working with diverse senior stakeholders in an interdisciplinary environment; and willing to work flexibly and to adapt to changing needs across the working groups. Applicants must have a first degree in a relevant topic. 

The post is part-time 21 hours per week, 0.6 FTE and fixed-term until 31 October 2028. The post is funded by the Wellcome Trust and is available from 01 November 2026. 

The salary will be on the LSHTM salary scale, Grade 5 in the range £40,784 - £45,173 per annum pro rata (inclusive of London Weighting). The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service. Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part-time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in London at LSHTM.

Applications should be made on-line via our jobs website. Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk. Please quote reference EPH-EPED-2026-10.

The supporting statement section should set out how your qualifications, experience and training meet each of the selection criteria. Please provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion. The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable. 

Please note that if you are shortlisted and are unable to attend on the interview date it may not be possible to offer you an alternative date.
